answer: Each agent keeps its reputation in a shared vault: every completed job adds a verifiable signal of honest work, and every dispute subtracts from it. New identities start with no history, so they must earn trust slowly, one attested job at a time. A Sybil attacker faces a pulse of real costs - each fake must do genuine, checkable work before it can transact - so cloning identities multiplies expense without multiplying influence.
